items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: Maynard Ferguson and his 13 angry men? ... Maynard Ferguson's an old name. He played with me, he played with Kenton.

ctx.x: Al was capable of playing, you know, a high lead, on up to an A or something, and the same thing like Maynard Ferguson's capable of doing that. He isn't just a guy that goes up and -- but Cat's a showboat, you know, and he's a jolly little fat man. I love him dearly. I've used him a few times. I went up to Canada here in '73, and I took him up there with me, and I said, "Now, look --," we used the CBC house orchestra up there. We had it one week -- I had it one week, and then Benny Goodman had it one week, and…

the greatest lip in the world, and he got up and he, splat, split, splat, splat, da-da, you know, and -- (Laughter) -- the guys in the band broke up. They recovered in time, but he of course acquitted himself nobly after that, but what an awful thing to happen after the buildup, and I had told him, now don't you do anything before you're introduced, because don't blow the game. And then we couldn't keep him out. He was into every arrangement, just playing everybody's parts.
